items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: who was camped there, but Redhill, Lieutenant Redhill, and Louie Kenricks, police. And I says to Louie, I said, what you doing here?

ctx.x: Well, that generation is forgotten today, pretty much. I know.

I know, but today, the generation and the musicians that they have now will never, and you can take that from me as an authority, will never play the music we used to play in our days. For the simple reason is that they didn't, they gave you a program. All right, you play according to the program. Now, that program maybe might have contained 12, 14, or 16 different type dances. Mazzucca, lances, shatters, waltzes, minuets, varieties. That was all on the program, and you played just the way the program was. Show…
Yeah, I'm gonna get a cigarette. Uh, I was wondering something. How did you get your start in music?
